post: fun call obs => (SolidCore.Verify.VC.stageScope SolidCore.Verify.VC.Token.fnTransfer [(2, 4096)] call → SolidCore.Verify.VC.Token.trPost call obs) ∧ (SolidCore.Verify.VC.stageScope SolidCore.Verify.VC.Token.fnBurn [(2, 4096)] call → SolidCore.Verify.VC.Token.burnPost call obs)
spec: solar-verify's Token spec (scripts/verify/Token.sol): transfer's three ensures clauses on distinct addresses (trPost) and burn's (burnPost), on success; the discharged obligations Contracts.Token.Discharge / VC.Burn
excluded: deployment: the init code is not covered; the statement is about the runtime bytecode from any storage that writes the slots the constructor writes
source model trusted: SolidCore's checked contract (the solc AST through scripts/solc_ast_to_lean_source.py and the type checker) is the meaning of the source (frontend trust boundary)
calls: one frame, caller 0x2000, contract at 0x1000, the block and transaction of Target.message; no external calls, GAS reads or return data in the code (the loop checker's fragment)
gas: the bound is the loop checker's (22100 per item times the final EVM IR's block fuel, plus memory), coarse; below it the bytecode may fail without effects, which equivalence admits

valid calls: transfer, burn, mint, totalSupply and owner ABI-encoded with clean argument words, no value, from any storage that writes slot 2 (owner); balanceOf (a public mapping getter outside the generic stage's fragment) and calls with value are outside the statement

assumption HashInj: keccak256 of (address, 0) is injective on addresses (the mapping's slots), a premise of the statement, not proved
